topic: AMD reports record data center earnings
headline_marked: [[AMD hits record $13.4B revenue]] in Q3 2026, driven by data center growth
headline: AMD hits record $13.4B revenue in Q3 2026, driven by data center growth
summary: AMD's data center business generated $8.5 billion, accounting for 63% of revenue, and is projected to exceed 80% of total company revenue beyond 2027. Meanwhile, its gaming business saw a 40% drop.
details: AMD announced its largest and most profitable quarter in history for Q3 2026, reporting a record $13.4 billion in quarterly revenue. This significant growth was primarily fueled by its data center business, which contributed $8.5 billion.

The company is projecting another record high next quarter, expecting to reach $17 billion in revenue. CEO Lisa Su stated that AMD anticipates its total revenue to grow more than 80 percent in 2027, with the data center segment being the largest contributor.

As of Q3 2026, the data center business already accounted for approximately 63 percent of AMD's net quarterly revenue. CFO Jean Hu further noted that beyond 2027, the data center business is expected to comprise over 80 percent of the company's total revenue.

In contrast to the booming data center sector, AMD's gaming business experienced a 40 percent year-over-year drop, falling to $773 million. This decline is attributed to price hikes in components like RAM, affecting PCs and game consoles due to high demand from AI data centers.

Su acknowledged that rising component prices impact overall system pricing, making consumer markets more sensitive. She added that AMD is planning for a "down year for 2027" in the consumer segment, reflecting the current market environment.

topic: pwa-debug lets Claude AI debug live browser apps
headline_marked: [[pwa-debug lets AI debug your live browser]] directly, including authenticated sessions
headline: pwa-debug lets AI debug your live browser directly, including authenticated sessions
summary: pwa-debug is an open-source tool that gives AI agents direct, structured access to your live, logged-in browser, including DOM, network, and service workers. It solves common PWA issues without manual intervention or screenshots.
details: pwa-debug is an open-source (MIT) server and browser extension designed to eliminate the manual loop of debugging web apps with AI assistants. It gives AI agents like Claude Code direct, structured access to your live, logged-in browser.

This tool covers the DOM, console, network, framework state, store state, service workers, caches, and storage. Crucially, it attaches to your normal browser profile, allowing the AI agent to see authenticated sessions and real service-worker states, unlike other tools that start a fresh, unauthenticated browser.

It directly addresses common PWA problems such as stale caches, service workers that won't update, install failures, and version skew. The tool reads runtime data without relying on screenshots or OCR, providing precise diagnostics.

Key PWA diagnostics include service-worker lifecycle and versions, CacheStorage contents, installability gaps with fixes, and a live capability matrix. The `pwa_update_analyze` tool combines SW status, cache ages, and 404s to diagnose issues like "cached HTML is older than the JS it references."

AI agents can interact with the page using commands like `pdl_click`, `pdl_fill`, `pdl_submit`, `pdl_navigate`, and various touch gestures. These events are dispatched as native-event sequences, ensuring proper firing in delegated event systems like React and Vue.

pwa-debug also supports mobile debugging by connecting to Android phones over adb and CDP, injecting the same page-world code. This enables all page tools, including React state, PWA diagnostics, and gestures, to work on phone tabs.

The `layout_sweep` function allows for comprehensive layout analysis across various viewports, color schemes, and app states. It measures pages for layout issues, grouping raw findings into distinct problems and providing screenshots.

Every tool returns a structured response including `ok`, `data`, `error?`, and `next_steps[]`, enabling the AI agent to recover from setup gaps and errors autonomously. `pdl_help` provides a full usage guide, with filters to keep responses concise.

pwa-debug is complementary to `chrome-devtools-mcp`; both can drive the same tab over separate channels. The setup process is agent-driven, with each step guiding the agent on what to do next based on the results.
Browser support includes Chromium-family browsers (Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Opera) and Android Chrome over adb. Brave and Chromium offer the smoothest experience.
